title: sftp is a second, divergent SSH stack: new connection per step, fully synchronous body, cancellation checked only before connect
existing_state: SftpCommand uses SSH.NET's SftpClient (SftpCommand.cs:5,66) — a completely separate stack from the Rebex SshShellSession/connection pool that powers send. Every sftp step constructs a fresh SftpClient with password-only auth and performs a full TCP connect + key exchange + auth (66-72), then disposes it — so a foreach uploading N files to a host pays N complete SSH handshakes, and a fleet run multiplies that by host count. The entire method is synchronous despite returning Task (ExecuteAsync has zero awaits, 15-103): Connect() (72), UploadFile (82) and DownloadFile (91) all block the worker thread, and the cancellation token is checked exactly once before connecting (64) — pressing Stop during a stuck connect or a large transfer does nothing until OperationTimeout fires (default 120s, 35, or much longer for a slow multi-GB transfer). Capability divergence breeds defects: hosts reachable via send (Rebex pool, key/Vault credentials via CredentialMode.Vault) fail on sftp because only username/password literals or context vars are accepted (111-137), with no key auth and no Vault path.
recommendation: Cache one connected SftpClient per host endpoint on ScriptContext (keyed host:port:user, disposed when the host scope ends) so loops reuse the connection instead of re-handshaking per step. Switch to SSH.NET's async surface: ConnectAsync(cancellationToken), and replace UploadFile/DownloadFile with sftp.Open(...) + Stream.CopyToAsync(buffer, cancellationToken) so Stop actually interrupts transfers. Route credential resolution through the same path the Rebex session uses (per-host vault_path column / CredentialMode.Vault) so sftp and send agree on how a host authenticates. Longer term, evaluate whether Rebex (already licensed and pooled) exposes SFTP so the second stack can be deleted entirely.
user_benefit: Bulk file transfers across a fleet stop paying a full SSH handshake per file, the Stop button works during transfers instead of hanging for up to the timeout, and scripts that authenticate via Vault/keys for send no longer mysteriously fail on sftp steps.

evidence.note: Task-returning method with zero awaits — fully synchronous body
single token check, then new SftpClient(host,port,user,password) + blocking Connect() per step
password-only credential resolution; no key or Vault integration
